h: Get the most out of your visit
p: A bit of planning goes a long way here. When you arrive, find out when the next planetarium shows are running and build the rest of your visit around them, because they're timed and the popular ones can fill up on busy days. School holidays and wet weekends are when the place is at its liveliest, so if you prefer a calmer wander, a term-time visit is a smart move.

Pace yourselves too. With so much to press, pull and test, younger children can burn out fast, so plan a snack stop halfway rather than trying to see the lot in one go. Older kids will want time at the trickier exhibits, so let them lead now and then.

Afterwards, Millennium Square itself is a nice place to let off steam, with its water features and the bronze statues dotted about, including Bristol-born Cary Grant. Bristol Aquarium sits right next door if you fancy doubling up, while M Shed, the city's free museum on Princes Wharf, is a short stroll along the water. Further round the harbour you'll find Brunel's SS Great Britain, and the harbour ferries are a fun way to hop between stops. College Green and Bristol Cathedral are only a few minutes away on foot, and Cabot Tower on Brandon Hill gives you cracking views back over the whole lot.
